Question B-007-002-004.

Why the correct answer is right: The D region is low and, in daylight, tends to absorb lower-HF energy instead of returning it usefully. That makes it the least helpful region for long-distance radio-wave propagation.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "The F2 region": F2 is high and is the main region behind the longest ordinary HF paths.
- sourceIndex 2: "The F1 region": F1 is part of the daytime F region and can participate in refraction. It is not the main daylight absorption problem.
- sourceIndex 3: "The E region": E can refract some signals and can produce sporadic-E openings, so it is not the least useful choice here.
